messages.subject: Posterior as prior
parts:
Dear Help,

I am trying to use first fits of a model for another fit of the same model, hoping that I will gain some computing time by doing so - the data used for the different fits is nearly the same. My model is negative binomial.

I have found how to give my own prior for the hyperparameter of the negative binomial likelihood. I use result$marginals.hyperpar$size for creating prior.table.

However, as regards the fixed effects, is it still so that one can only change the mean and the precision of the Gaussian prior and cannot give any other distribution as prior?

Thanks a lot in advance.

Best wishes

Maëlle.

parts:
On Thu, 2014-09-25 at 01:50 -0700, Maëlle Salmon wrote:
> Dear Help,
>
> I am trying to use first fits of a model for another fit of the same
> model, hoping that I will gain some computing time by doing so - the
> data used for the different fits is nearly the same. My model is
> negative binomial.
>
> I have found how to give my own prior for the hyperparameter of the
> negative binomial likelihood. I use result$marginals.hyperpar$size for
> creating prior.table.

Hi,

if the model is the same (wrt the hyperparameters), then there is an
*experimental* feature which allows you to use the posterior from some
data as the (joint) prior for the next. This only referes to the
hyperparameters.

I attach a small example doing this, where I compare the results doing
one block of data at the same, with the result achived using all the
data. (which should be the same).

> However, as regards the fixed effects, is it still so that one can
> only change the mean and the precision of the Gaussian prior and
> cannot give any other distribution as prior?

fixed effects can only be given a Gaussian prior, yes.
